lab03-s000.title: Before You Begin
lab03-s000.markdown:
**Estimated time:** 15 minutes
**What you will create:** A gross profit sheet. Use Fabric to work backward from a $12.5 million gross profit target to a combination of revenue and cost of goods sold. ---

lab03-s001.title: Where This Module Fits
lab03-s001.markdown:
The revenue target is $30 million. Management also wants **$12.5 million in gross profit**, but you do not yet know whether these two targets are compatible.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **This exercise aims to achieve the gross profit target.** Its input is the bottom-up `2026 Sales Plan` from Module 02, not the separate $30 million `2026 Target` column. Achieving $12.5 million in gross profit does not mean you have simultaneously achieved $30 million in revenue. To pursue both, design the conditions accordingly, for example by adding the revenue target as a constraint.

Previously, you might have repeatedly tried increasing revenue a little, reducing cost of goods sold (COGS) a little, and recalculating. Optimizer helps you search for a suitable combination.

lab03-s002.title: How Optimizer Works
lab03-s002.markdown:
Optimizer is **multivariable goal seeking**. Rather than rearranging a formula to produce an answer in one step, it is a solver that searches for a solution iteratively. Each iteration performs these steps:

1. Assign trial values to the inputs.
2. Recalculate the resulting measure.
3. Compare the result with the target.
4. Adjust the inputs and repeat.

This continues until the result is within the target tolerance or the iteration limit is reached. You therefore cannot predetermine the adjustment proportions for the two inputs. Multiple combinations may also achieve the same target.

You need the following three elements:

| Element | Used in this module |
|---|---|
| **Independent variables:** Inputs you allow to change | `Sales Plan` and `COGS`, for which you create editable copies in Step 2 |
| **Dependent measure:** Formula measure to solve for | `Gross Profit`, created in Step 3 |
| **Objective:** Reach a specified value, maximize, or minimize | Target value `12.5m` |

There are two operating modes. **Target-based** searches for inputs that achieve a specified number; you will use it in this exercise. **Direction-based** maximizes or minimizes, supporting questions such as, “How high can profit go while respecting these constraints?”

Other applications include finding the sales volume and price required for a revenue target, reductions by expense category to stay within budget, or adjustments to collection and payment terms to secure a target cash balance.

---

lab03-s003.title: Step 1: Create a Gross Profit Sheet
lab03-s003.markdown:
1. On the **Home** ribbon, select **New Planning Sheet**. If **Confirm Action** appears for unsaved changes, select **Save and Proceed** and wait for saving to complete. Set the name to `Gross Profit` and select **Create**.

   ![New Planning Sheet with Gross Profit entered in Name](../assets/screenshots/lab03/01-gross-profit-create.png)

   ![Explorer containing two sheets, with empty Rows, Columns, and Values for Gross Profit](../assets/screenshots/lab03/02-gross-profit-created.png)


2. Assign the following fields. **Configure two measures from different sources in Values.**

   | Field | Value | Source |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Rows** | *Region* → *Category* → *Sub Category* | *Geography*, then *Product* |
   | **Columns** | *Year* → *Quarter* → *Month Short* | *Date* |
   | **Values** (first) | *2026 Sales Plan* | **From Sheets** → *Plan Intro* |
   | **Values** (second) | *2025 COGS* | *Measures Table* |

   Drag each field directly from the **Data** pane to **Rows / Columns / Values** in **Fields**. Expand **From Sheets**, then open **Plan Intro** within it to see **2026 Target** and **2026 Sales Plan**, created in Module 02. Select **2026 Sales Plan** here. Next, expand **Measures Table** and add **2025 COGS** to **Values**.

   ![Plan Intro expanded under From Sheets, listing 2026 Target and 2026 Sales Plan](../assets/screenshots/lab03/09-from-sheets-options.png)

   ![Immediately after assigning 2026 Sales Plan, showing Sum of 2026... in Values and a checkmark at its source](../assets/screenshots/lab03/10-sales-from-sheets.png)


   <details>
   <summary>Screens showing assignment of the row and column fields</summary>

   ![Region from Geography assigned to Rows](../assets/screenshots/lab03/03-region-assigned.png)

   ![Category from Product assigned as the second level of Rows](../assets/screenshots/lab03/04-category-assigned.png)

   ![Rows ordered Region, Category, Sub Category](../assets/screenshots/lab03/05-rows-assigned.png)

   ![Year from Date assigned to Columns](../assets/screenshots/lab03/06-year-assigned.png)

   ![Quarter from Date assigned as the second level of Columns](../assets/screenshots/lab03/07-quarter-assigned.png)

   ![Columns ordered Year, Quarter, Month Short](../assets/screenshots/lab03/08-columns-assigned.png)

   </details>

   > If **Failed to refresh data after blend update** appears, do not continue until the display recovers. Check the sources, field placement, and error details.

   ![Intermediate screen immediately after adding 2025 COGS, showing a refresh error and Processing Data](../assets/screenshots/lab03/11-sales-and-cogs-assigned.png)

3. Double-click **Sum of 2026 Sales Plan** in **Values**. Replace the inline text with `2026 Sales Plan` and press **Enter**. This changes the reference measure's display name in this sheet.

   ![Renaming the reference measure to 2026 Sales Plan in the Values inline editor](../assets/screenshots/lab03/12-rename-source-measure.png)

   In the sample data, the **2025** All row displays revenue of approximately **26.10 in Millions** and cost of approximately **14,166.31 in Thousands**. You will create the **Sales Plan** copy column in the next step.

> [!TIP]
> **From Sheets** connects planning sheets within the same Plan item. You can reference the sales plan created in Module 02 as an input to this sheet. Changes to the original sheet are reflected here too, avoiding copy-and-paste and version mismatches.

lab03-s004.title: Step 2: Create Editable Input Columns
lab03-s004.markdown:
Optimizer needs columns whose values you allow it to change. Measures retrieved from another sheet or a semantic model are read-only.

1. On the **Planning** ribbon, select **Number** → **Copy from another series** → **2026 Sales Plan**.

   ![Copy from another series under Number listing 2026 Sales Plan and 2025 COGS, with values for both also visible in the grid](../assets/screenshots/lab03/13-copy-sales-menu.png)

   If **Save changes to proceed** appears, select **Save and continue**, then wait for saving to finish and the copy settings to open. When switching sheets, the wording may instead be **Save and Proceed**.

   ![Save changes to proceed prompt before copying, requesting a save through Save and continue](../assets/screenshots/lab03/14-save-before-copy.png)

   **Select and delete all existing text in Title**, then enter only `Sales Plan`. Verify **Visual Measure / Number / Column aggregation type: Sum / Row aggregation type: Sum / Distribute parent value to children: checked**, and select **Create**.

   ![Copy settings showing Title Sales Plan, Visual Measure, Number, Sum/Sum, and parent-value distribution](../assets/screenshots/lab03/15-sales-copy-settings.png)

   ![Editable Sales Plan added alongside the two source columns, showing All 26.10M](../assets/screenshots/lab03/16-sales-copy-created.png)

2. Select **Number** → **Copy from another series** → **2025 COGS**. Delete the existing Title text, enter `COGS`, verify the same **Visual Measure / Number / Sum / Sum / parent-value distribution enabled** settings, and select **Create**.

   ![COGS copy settings showing Title COGS and the aggregation and distribution settings](../assets/screenshots/lab03/17-cogs-copy-settings.png)

> [!NOTE]
> **Title** contains an automatically generated name. Remove it before typing. Leave the other settings at the defaults explained in [Module 02](02-allocation-and-collaboration.md).

You now have editable copies of both inputs to adjust. The original measures remain as baselines for later comparison. That comparison becomes important at the end of the module.

**Check before proceeding.** The grid should contain these **four** measure columns:

| Column | Source | Editable? |
|---|---|---|
| 2026 Sales Plan | From Sheets, Plan Intro | No |
| 2025 COGS | Measures Table | No |
| **Sales Plan** | Copy you created | **Yes** |
| **COGS** | Copy you created | **Yes** |

![Four columns comprising original references and editable copies, with matching All revenue of 26.10M and cost of 14,166.31K](../assets/screenshots/lab03/18-four-series-stable.png)

In the sample data, both the original **2026 Sales Plan** and copied **Sales Plan** show approximately **26.10M** on the All row. Both the original **2025 COGS** and copied **COGS** show approximately **14,166.31K**. If you inspect additional digits in the edit bar, close it with **Escape** without changing the value.

![Sales Plan annual grand total opened to read 26095900.2404 in the edit bar](../assets/screenshots/lab03/19-copy-sales-baseline-precision.png)

In the sample data, the COGS annual grand total is **14166310.36**. Close with **Escape** without changing the value.

![Copied COGS annual grand total opened to read 14166310.36 in the edit bar; the Gross Profit column created later is also visible](../assets/screenshots/lab03/28-copy-cogs-baseline-precision.png)

If there are only two columns, Step 2 has not taken effect. Without the copies, the formula in Step 3 cannot reference the required columns.

lab03-s005.title: Step 3: Calculate Gross Profit
lab03-s005.markdown:
1. Select **Formula** on the **Planning** ribbon to open the **Formula Measure** pane. In this example, the defaults were Title **New Measure**, **Visual Measure / Number**, **Column aggregation type: Sum**, and **Row aggregation type: Formula**.

   ![Initial Formula Measure settings, showing column aggregation Sum and row aggregation Formula](../assets/screenshots/lab03/20-formula-defaults.png)
2. Configure the following:

   | Field | Value | Notes |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Title** | `Gross Profit` | Remove the existing name before entering it |
   | **Insert as** | Visual Measure | The default is appropriate for this exercise |
   | **Data type** | Number | The default |
   | **Formula** | `[Sales Plan] - [COGS]` | Select the editable **Sales Plan** and **COGS** from **References**, joining them with the ASCII operator ` - ` |
   | **Column aggregation type** | **Formula** | **The default is Sum. Be sure to change it** |
   | **Row aggregation type** | Formula | Already set to this by default |

   Open the **Column aggregation type** dropdown and change **Sum** to **Formula**.

   ![Column aggregation dropdown containing Formula, with Sum initially selected](../assets/screenshots/lab03/21-column-aggregation-options.png)


   ![References suggestions opened by typing S, listing 2026 Sales Plan and Sales Plan](../assets/screenshots/lab03/23-formula-reference-candidates.png)

   ![Typing C after the subtraction operator, showing 2025 COGS and COGS suggestions](../assets/screenshots/lab03/24-formula-cogs-reference.png)

   Confirm that the displayed expression is **`[Sales Plan] - [COGS]`** and both column and row aggregation are **Formula**, then select **Create**.

   ![Final settings with the expression selected through References and Formula for both column and row aggregation](../assets/screenshots/lab03/25-formula-references-configured.png)

   The pane may stay open after creation, with the button changing from **Create** to **Update**. Once the new **Gross Profit** column and calculated results appear in the grid, close the pane using **×** at its top right. Do not select Create repeatedly simply because the pane remains open.

   ![After creating Gross Profit, the pane is in Update editing mode and All shows 11,929.59K](../assets/screenshots/lab03/26-formula-created-update-pane.png)

   ![Pane closed, showing five columns: two originals, two input copies, and Gross Profit](../assets/screenshots/lab03/27-gross-profit-result.png)

   > If **Parse error** appears, clear the formula field and reselect the two editable columns from **References**. Even if the expression looks identical, verify that the columns are bound by selecting the reference suggestions.

   ![Parse error shown when typing a formula without selecting columns from References](../assets/screenshots/lab03/22-formula-typed-syntax-error.png)

> [!TIP]
> Starting to type in **Formula** opens a suggestion list with two tabs. **References** lists columns in this sheet, such as *2026 Sales Plan*, as well as dimension members such as *2025*, *GrandTotal*, *Category*, *Month Short*, and *Quarter*. **Functions** lists built-in functions.
>
> Select existing columns from **References**. Choosing suggestions helps distinguish original columns from copies with similar names. If an expand icon appears, you can edit the formula in a larger editor.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **The Column aggregation default is Sum. Change it to Formula.** Row aggregation defaults to Formula, so pay particular attention to the column setting.
>
> If left as Sum, quarters and grand totals sum child values rather than recalculating `[Sales Plan] - [COGS]` at each level. With simple subtraction, the total can look correct, making this easy to miss. The same configuration mistake on margin or ratio rows produces inappropriate aggregates.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Reference the editable copies, not the original measures.** Both appear in the suggestions, with similar names.
>
> | Select | Do not select |
> |---|---|
> | `Sales Plan`: Copy created in Step 2 | `2026 Sales Plan`: Read-only source data |
> | `COGS`: Copy created in Step 2 | `2025 COGS`: Semantic model measure |
>
> Optimizer can adjust only editable data input columns. A formula referencing the original measures leaves it with no adjustable inputs. The two original columns are to remain unchanged for comparison at the end.

3. Open **Totals** on the **Planning** ribbon and change the **Column Grand Total** dropdown from **Off** to **Left**.

   ![Totals with Column Grand Total initially Off](../assets/screenshots/lab03/29-totals-off.png)

   ![Selecting Left from the Column Grand Total options Left, Right, and Off](../assets/screenshots/lab03/30-grand-total-left-option.png)

   Next, **right-click the row label** *Americas*. Hover over **Collapse** and select **Category** from the **Specific Level** dropdown in its submenu.

   ![Opening Specific Level under Collapse in the row menu and selecting Category](../assets/screenshots/lab03/31-category-level-options.png)

   ![After selecting Category, category rows collapsed with + icons; the context menu remains open](../assets/screenshots/lab03/32-category-collapsed-result.png)

   Both the **Grand Total** and **2025** groups show five series: two originals, two copies, and gross profit. In the sample data, All-row gross profit is approximately **11,929.59K**.

> [!NOTE]
> Display units may differ by column, for example Sales Plan *in Millions* and COGS *in Thousands*. This is a formatting difference. Formulas calculate from the underlying values, so do not subtract the displayed numbers directly without accounting for their units.

Before proceeding, record **All**-row Gross Profit. In the sample data example, revenue **26,095,900.2404** − COGS **14,166,310.36** = Gross Profit **11,929,589.8804**. In thousands to two decimal places, this is **11,929.59K**; the gap to the $12.5 million target is **570,410.1196**.

The original source's **12,144.89 thousands** and approximately **$355K** target gap are conditional examples for a further increase in Module 02's sales plan. Distinguish them from your current inputs.

> [!TIP]
> **Displayed numbers depend on the input plan.** The following is a run using the sample data. Observe how the two inputs change to bring Gross Profit toward the $12.5 million target.

Confirm the formula is configured correctly using these two checks:

- The sheet title lists the five columns *2026 Sales Plan, 2025 COGS, Sales Plan, COGS, Gross Profit*.
- Gross Profit on each row equals that row's Sales Plan minus COGS. In the sample data, All-row gross profit is **11,929,589.8804**, or **11,929.59K** in thousands to two decimal places. Do not directly subtract displays in millions and thousands.

lab03-s006.title: Step 4: Run Optimizer
lab03-s006.markdown:
Optimizer is a three-stage wizard: **Objective & Variables**, **Add Constraints**, and **Output**.

1. Select the **Gross Profit** cell in the **Grand Total** group on the **All** row, then select **Optimize** on the **Planning** ribbon. This command is gray and unavailable until you select a valid target cell.

   ![Initial Optimizer Objective and Target Value settings](../assets/screenshots/lab03/33-optimizer-objective-initial.png)
2. In **Objective & Variables**, set **Objective** to `Target` and **Target Value** to `12.5m`.

   Confirm that **GrandTotal** and **Gross Profit** appear below as the calculation target. Expand **Show Formula** if needed to inspect the formula.

3. Under **Variables to Update**, open **Choose Series** and select both `Sales Plan` and `COGS`. **Next** remains disabled until at least one series is selected.

   ![Target 12.5m and COGS and Sales Plan options in Choose Series during the run](../assets/screenshots/lab03/34-optimizer-variable-options.png)

   ![COGS and Sales Plan both checked, with Next enabled](../assets/screenshots/lab03/35-optimizer-configured.png)
4. Select **Next**.
5. In **Add Constraints**, confirm **No Constraints Added**. In this basic exercise, do not add constraints; select **Run** once.

   ![Add Constraints showing No Constraints Added, ready to execute with Run](../assets/screenshots/lab03/36-optimizer-no-constraints.png)
6. In **Output**, confirm **Target Value** is 12.50m and check the run status and **Achieved** value. If Tolerance is 0.1%, the tolerance relative to the target is $12,500, giving an arithmetic achieved-value range of 12,487,500–12,512,500. Alongside status indicators such as a green checkmark, verify the actual settings and values at their original precision. The display will not necessarily round to 12.50m. The adjacent **Variables** panel shows the input values found by the solver.
   ![Output showing Target Value and Achieved both 12.50m, proposed inputs, and default parameters](../assets/screenshots/lab03/37-optimizer-output.png)

   In the sample run, **Target Value: 12.50m / Achieved: 12.50m**, with proposed inputs of **Sales Plan: approximately 26.38m / COGS: approximately 13.88m**. These displays are examples in millions to two decimal places. Also check tolerance and run status.

7. After checking the settings and result, select **Apply** once. In the sample data example, **Sales Plan** is approximately **26.38M**, **COGS** approximately **13,881.11K**, and **Gross Profit** approximately **12,500.00K**.

   ![After Apply, Sales Plan edit bar 26381105.29986 and changed copy columns and gross profit; Saving values is an intermediate indicator](../assets/screenshots/lab03/38-optimized-sales-precision.png)

   ![After Apply, COGS edit bar 13881105.29986 and All gross profit 12,500.00K](../assets/screenshots/lab03/39-optimized-cogs-precision.png)

   ![Applied sheet with editor closed; the allocation menu obscures the start of Grand Total gross profit, and the non-editing bar shows COGS 13881105.299862](../assets/screenshots/lab03/40-optimized-result.png)

   To inspect inputs, read the copied columns' edit bars, then close with **Escape** without changing or reconfirming the values. Saving and reloading are separate operations.

The **Set Parameters** panel on the right provides three tuning settings. Defaults are **Strategy: Balanced**, **Tolerance: Standard (0.1%)**, and **Iterations: Standard (200 tries)**. A **Re-Run** button appears below them. Leave the defaults unless the target is not reached. Guidance on changing them appears later in this module.

> [!NOTE]
> If input series are missing from **Choose Series**, check that you created editable copies in Step 2. **Standard (200 tries)** is the configured maximum iteration count; it does not mean the solver actually runs 200 iterations.

lab03-s007.title: Step 5: Review What Changed
lab03-s007.markdown:
1. Confirm that the original **2026 Sales Plan** and **2025 COGS** are visible. If hidden, display them using **Show Columns** on the **Planning** ribbon.

   **Single-click** each original grand total cell and inspect the pre-optimization value in the read-only formula bar. In the sample data, revenue is **26095900.2404** and COGS is **14166310.36**.

   ![Original 2026 Sales Plan annual amount 26095900.2404 still shown in the formula bar after optimization](../assets/screenshots/lab03/41-source-sales-retained-after-optimize.png)

   ![Original 2025 COGS annual amount 14166310.36 also retained, with only the copy columns and gross profit changed](../assets/screenshots/lab03/42-source-cogs-retained-after-optimize.png)

   ![Show Columns confirming the original 2026 Sales Plan and 2025 COGS are checked](../assets/screenshots/lab03/45-show-columns-checked.png)

   In the copy columns, selecting the cells lets you check the adjusted revenue **26381105.299862** and cost **13881105.299862**. The number of digits displayed varies by UI.

   ![Sales Plan selected, showing 26381105.299862 in the non-editing formula bar](../assets/screenshots/lab03/43-optimized-sales-selected-full.png)

   ![COGS selected, showing 13881105.299862 in the non-editing formula bar](../assets/screenshots/lab03/44-optimized-cogs-selected-full-correct.png)

   The following table gives example before-and-after values for this sample data.

   | Item | Before optimization | Example after Apply | Change |
   |---|---:|---:|---:|
   | Sales Plan | 26095900.2404 | 26381105.299862 | +285205.059462 |
   | COGS | 14166310.36 | 13881105.299862 | −285205.060138 |
   | Gross Profit calculated as the difference | 11929589.8804 | 12500000.000000 | +570410.119600 |

   Gross Profit in the sample data is **12,500,000**. This falls within the 0.1% tolerance range of **12,487,500–12,512,500** around the 12,500,000 target.

You can compare the original and optimized columns side by side.

In this sample data example, the proposal increases revenue by approximately $285,000 and reduces cost by approximately $285,000. Use these concrete amounts to assess whether the responsible departments can deliver them.

<details>
<summary>Conditional arithmetic example from the original source</summary>

The following table is a **conditional arithmetic example from the original source**. It illustrates closing a gap of roughly $355,000 from approximately $12.14 million in gross profit; the solver does not necessarily return these values.

| Input | Before | After | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sales Plan | $26,311.20K | **$26,488.75K** | Approximately +$177.55K |
| COGS | $14,166.31K | **$13,988.75K** | Approximately −$177.56K |
| **Gross Profit** | $12,144.89K | **$12,500.00K** | **Approximately +$355.11K** |

> [!NOTE]
> **The original source's “revenue increase +$179K” does not exactly match the other numbers.** With COGS of 13,988.75K and gross profit of 12,500.00K, revenue is 26,488.75K. The table above is a conditional arithmetic example, not a guarantee of Optimizer output.

Gross Profit in this calculation is exactly 12,500.00K. Evaluate actual runs against the configured tolerance.

In this conditional calculation, the improvement splits roughly equally between revenue growth and cost reduction. This is not a rule that the actual solver always allocates 50:50. Numbers also vary with the plan produced in Module 02. Here, focus on the relationship: a small revenue increase and a small cost reduction bring gross profit to the target.

This conditional arithmetic example gives management concrete amounts to discuss: **approximately $178,000 more revenue and $178,000 less cost**. Assign owners to assess feasibility against business constraints.

> [!NOTE]
> The original screen example displayed Sales Plan in millions to two decimal places; 26.49 was a rounded form of a more detailed value. The original source's conditional calculation table uses thousands to two decimal places for easier comparison. Subtracting displayed values alone can differ from the formula result at original precision. For millions to two decimal places, the rounding half-width is $5,000, so check the underlying values when reconciling actual results.

</details>

<details>

![Americas optimized COGS: 3887233.624033](../assets/screenshots/lab03/47-americas-optimized-cogs.png)

lab03-s009.title: Save and Reload
lab03-s009.markdown:
1. Select **Save** and wait for the Saving indicator to disappear and saving to complete. Reload the browser, wait for actual data to display, then review the result in **Reading** mode.

   ![Reading mode after saving and reloading, retaining five series, All gross profit 12,500.00K, Grand Total/2025, and expanded Skin Care](../assets/screenshots/lab03/53-optimizer-reloaded-reading.png)

   In the sample data example, All displays original revenue **26.10M**, original COGS **14,166.31K**, copied revenue **26.38M**, copied COGS **13,881.11K**, and gross profit **12,500.00K**.

2. Return to **Editing** and double-click each copy column's annual grand total. Read the edit-bar value, then close with **Escape** without confirming a change.

   ![Sales Plan edit bar after reload: 26381105.29986, matching the five-decimal edit value before saving](../assets/screenshots/lab03/54-sales-reloaded-editor.png)

   ![COGS edit bar after reload: 13881105.29986, also matching the five-decimal edit value before saving](../assets/screenshots/lab03/55-cogs-reloaded-editor.png)

After reloading, confirm that representative values and edit values match those before saving. The number of edit-value digits varies by UI.

lab03-s010.title: When You Need Constraints
lab03-s010.markdown:
The **Add Constraints** page supports two types of constraints:

- **Range-based:** Specify lower and upper input limits and search for a solution within that range. For example, use this to limit COGS reductions to 2% based on an agreement with procurement.
- **Fixed-value:** Fix a particular input and achieve the target through other inputs. For example, if the annual price is finalized, fix price and adjust sales volume.

To add a range-based constraint, select the target series and **Set Type: Range** in **Add Constraints**, set **Min / Max**, then select **Apply** on that constraint card. To constrain another series, use **+ Add** to add a card and configure it the same way. **Apply** here confirms a constraint. Verify each card reflects its settings before selecting **Run** or **Re-Run**. **Apply** in **Output** is a different operation: it writes the reviewed proposed values to the planning sheet. Do not select Output's Apply before checking target and constraint status.

#### Optional Exercise: Set Two Range Constraints

Open Optimizer while retaining the existing optimization result, and set **Target Value** to `12.6m`. In **Add Constraints**, choose **Set Type: Range** for COGS, enter **Min: 13700000 / Max: 13900000**, and select **Apply** on that constraint card. Use **+ Add** to add a Sales Plan constraint card, set **Range / Min: 26000000 / Max: 27000000**, and select its **Apply**. Confirm that both ranges are displayed, then select **Run** and read the achieved value, run status, and proposed values that satisfy the constraints in Output.

![Example COGS Range constraint card with Min 13,700,000 / Max 13,900,000](../assets/screenshots/lab03/optimizer-range-constraint-example.png)

**Apply** within a card confirms a constraint. **Apply** in **Output** writes proposed values to the plan. In this optional exercise, close without selecting **Apply** in Output, and confirm at the same precision that existing inputs and gross profit are unchanged. Output depends on the environment and initial values, so do not use a fixed achieved value as the pass criterion.

Without constraints, a proposal may be mathematically valid but operationally infeasible. Reaching the target with a 20% cost reduction is not a usable plan if procurement cannot deliver it.

lab03-s011.title: If the Target Is Not Reached
lab03-s011.markdown:
The target may not be reached, for example when constraints are tight. You can adjust the following three settings in **Set Parameters** on the Output page, then select **Re-Run**.

| Parameter | Default | What it adjusts |
|---|---|---|
| **Strategy** | Balanced | The size of each adjustment. Smaller steps converge more slowly but are less likely to overshoot the target. Larger steps advance faster but may jump past a solution |
| **Tolerance** | Standard, 0.1% | How close to the target counts as complete. For a 12.5m target, a 0.1% tolerance gives a range of 12.4875m–12.5125m |
| **Iterations** | Standard, 200 tries | The number of repetitions permitted before calculation stops |

If no solution is found, first consider whether the target itself is unattainable under the constraints. Check feasibility before widening tolerance just to obtain a result.

---

lab03-s012.title: What You Have Accomplished
lab03-s012.markdown:
In this module, you use Optimizer to explore revenue and cost adjustments toward a $12.5 million gross profit target. Results depend on inputs, constraints, and tolerance; they do not mean the $30 million revenue target has also been achieved.

A year does not always unfold as planned. In Module 04, you will create a forecast that is updated as actuals change.

lab03-s013.title: Knowledge Check
lab03-s013.markdown:
1. Why did you copy *2026 Sales Plan* and *2025 COGS* before optimization?
2. What problems can arise if you leave formula-column aggregation settings at their defaults without checking both rows and columns?
3. Optimizer returned a 20% COGS reduction, but procurement says it is impossible. What should you have configured beforehand?
4. Two people complete this module and achieve $12.5 million in gross profit with different Sales Plan and COGS values. Did one of them do something wrong?

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. Optimizer can adjust only editable data input columns. Measures from another sheet or a semantic model are read-only.
2. An aggregation set to Sum rather than Formula sums child values instead of recalculating the formula at each level. Subtotals and grand totals for margins or ratios may become inappropriate. In this exercise, the column default is Sum and the row default is Formula.
3. On **Add Constraints**, you should have specified allowable input ranges or added fixed-value constraints.
4. No. Optimizer is an iterative solver, not a formula returning a unique answer. Multiple input combinations can achieve the same target, and starting values and adjustment sizes affect which combination is reached.

</details>
